title: finding(plugin-charts): the scatter branch bypasses `yAxisSpecProps`, so a spec `min`/`max`/`logarithmic`/`ticks`/`title` on its y-axis is silently dropped
body:
Found while pre-dispatch verification of objectui#7396 (that card is the scatter's *visual* edge clipping). This is a different defect on the same two axes, with a different blast radius, so it is filed rather than swept in.

## What

`AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` derives every spec-driven y-axis prop in one helper:

```
/** Recharts props derived from one spec y-axis (domain / scale / ticks / label). */
const yAxisSpecProps = React.useCallback((axis: NormalizedAxis | undefined, side: 'left' | 'right' = 'left') => {
  if (!axis) return {};
  const domain = domainFor(axis);
  const ticks = ticksFor(axis, axisValues(side));
  return {
    ...(ticks ? { ticks } : {}),
    ...(domain ? { domain } : {}),
    // `allowDataOverflow` is what makes an explicit domain actually clip
    // rather than being silently widened to fit the data.
    ...(domain ? { allowDataOverflow: true } : {}),
    ...(axis.logarithmic ? { scale: 'log' as const, domain: domain ?? ([1, 'auto'] as any) } : {}),
    ...(axis.title ? { label: { value: axis.title, angle: -90, position: 'insideLeft' as const } } : {}),
  };
}, [axisValues]);
```

**The scatter branch does not spread it.** Measured on `main` at `15b33aeb4`:

| probe | reading |
|---|---|
| SUBJECT — `yAxisSpecProps(` spread sites in the file | **5** — lines 1918, 1919, 2016, 2035, 2045 |
| SUBJECT — is the scatter YAxis (lines 1839-1847) among them | **no** |
| CONTROL — the helper exists and is reachable from the scatter branch's own component | **yes**, declared at line 1264 in the same component |

The scatter YAxis, verbatim at lines 1839-1847, carries `type`, `dataKey`, `name`, `tickLine`, `axisLine`, `tickFormatter` and `width` — and nothing derived from the spec axis. Its XAxis (lines 1831-1837) likewise.

## Cost — this one is a silent wrong answer, not a visual one

Five spec keys are accepted by the schema, normalized by `normalizeChartSchema`, and then **dropped on the floor for exactly one chart family**:

- `min` / `max` — an author who pins a y domain gets the auto domain instead. The chart is drawn to a scale the author did not ask for, and nothing refuses.
- `logarithmic` — a log axis renders linear.
- `ticks` — explicit tick values are ignored.
- `title` — the axis label never appears.

⭐ The discriminating property versus objectui#7396: there, the data is right and half a symbol is painted outside the plot box, which a reader can see. Here the picture is **confidently wrong** — a correct-looking chart at a scale the author overrode, with no diagnostic anywhere. An author who sets `min: 0` to stop a truncated-baseline reading gets the truncated baseline back, silently.

## Expected

The scatter's numeric axes go through the same derivation every other family uses, or the file states in writing why scatter is exempt.

## Not in objectui#7396's scope, deliberately

objectui#7396 is p3 and purely visual. Its dispatch order names this card as out of scope, so the two do not get merged into one diff by accident. ⛔ Whichever lands first must not silently absorb the other: an explicit padding domain on those axes and a spec-derived domain are the same prop, and a fix for one that ignores the other will shadow it.

## Not verified here

⛔ Whether any authored chart in this repository's corpus or in a downstream project actually sets `min` / `max` / `logarithmic` / `ticks` / `title` on a scatter y-axis is **not measured** — this card is the declaration-side reading only. A grader may want that liveness count before pricing it.
